builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: BenchMeUp: Building Software Engineering Benchmarks from Natural-Language Specifications
summary: The method replaces manual, labor-intensive benchmark construction (finding instances, preparing execution environments, establishing expected outcomes) with an automated pipeline of parallel LLM agents driven by natural-language specifications. It costs approximately $0.79 in LLM API calls and 36 minutes of wall-clock time per instance, plus the engineering complexity of setting up the validation harness and execution environments. Even after adoption, approximately 9% of constructed instances fail manual validity checks against the source, specification, or expected outcome, and 4% of packaged instances fail to support end-to-end evaluation, necessitating ongoing human validation.
rationale: The technique automates a costly manual process using accessible LLM APIs, but the 9% residual validity failure rate requires a manual review gate before production use.

claims.statement: The method replaces manual, labor-intensive benchmark construction (finding instances, preparing execution environments, establishing expected outcomes) with an automated pipeline of parallel LLM agents driven by natural-language specifications. It costs approximately $0.79 in LLM API calls and 36 minutes of wall-clock time per instance, plus the engineering complexity of setting up the validation harness and execution environments. Even after adoption, approximately 9% of constructed instances fail manual validity checks against the source, specification, or expected outcome, and 4% of packaged instances fail to support end-to-end evaluation, necessitating ongoing human validation.

BenchMeUp constructs benchmark instances for an average of $0.79 and 36 minutes per instance, with 91% of constructed instances (180/198) meeting all validity criteria, compared to 5% (10/200) for a general-purpose coding agent baseline.
